plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white blossoms push up through frost and leaf litter. Each one has a small green mark on its inner petals. Whole woodland floors turn white in drifts, and the flowers are a quiet sign that winter is loosening its grip.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, and sometimes earlier in mild winters
plants.location: Woodlands, churchyards and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein in their tissues. The plant also gave science galantamine, a compound used in medicines for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry rose-like blooms of layered petals around a boss of golden stamens. They flower when most of the garden is bare. The flowers stand out against the dark, polished leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter into early spring, typically January through April
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China, and widely grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In Japan the camellia is a classic winter flower. Its blooms usually fall whole, with the petals still attached, rather than dropping petal by petal.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise above arching strap-like leaves and carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. Each cluster looks like a firework held in place. The blooms are a rich blue-violet in the middle of the southern summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern summer, mainly December to February
plants.location: Native to the coastal Eastern Cape of South Africa, and widely grown in gardens in Australia, New Zealand and other warm regions
plants.funFact: The name comes from Greek words meaning love flower. Despite the common name, it isn't a true lily. It belongs to the amaryllis family.
